reasons: narrow: As stated, the theorem quantifies over an empty certifiable feasible set. In that case the certificate definition would require rational numbers satisfying inequalities against an infimum of plus infinity and a supremum of minus infinity, which is impossible. Restricting termination and finite endpoint enclosures to the nonempty-feasible regime is necessary. This does not weaken the advertised containment: whenever the target fiber is nonempty on \(p_0\in C_n\), it itself makes the confidence-feasible set nonempty, while an empty target fiber is contained trivially.
REVIEW: assume-the-crux narrowing — a new assume/suppose premise may promote the open obligation into a hypothesis (state the result and leave the construction an open obligation instead)

verdict.note: Reject global nonemptiness narrowing as assume-the-crux; retain other solver proof progress. Re-solve the theorem with unconditional checked feasibility/infeasibility branching and conditional finite endpoint interval.
